messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary cluster r4 reported p95/p99 regression for inference-service v2.1.7 after release at 1951234500. Symptoms: increased latency, elevated tail errors, kernel fallback observed in logs. Auto-paging to #incidents.

maya: saw the alert, jumping in. which canary? r4?

sam: yes r4-canary. spike started ~3m after traffic shift. p99 from ~180ms -> 1.4s, throughput dropped ~30%.

jordan: logs show repeated fallback to generic kernels on GPU nodes: "kernel_dispatch: fallback_to_generic=true reason=missing_optimized_kernel". Also saw batching throughput drop — small batch sizes spiking.

lee: confirming. KV cache warmups failing for some hot prefixes — 503s for ~0.8% of requests. stack traces point to new batching optimizer in v2.1.7.

katie: tagging the oncall: @sam you are oncall today?

sam: I'm oncall. paged. quick triage: is this a config or model code path? we rolled a runtime optimization and a batching heuristic tweak.

maya: timeline: deploy started 1951234400, canary traffic ramped to 10% -> regression seen after ramp to 30%. Rollout paused automatically at 30% by rollout-controller.

sam: immediate mitigation plan: 1) flip kill-switch to disable new batching heuristic 2) route canary traffic back to previous runtime binary 3) scale canary pool by +2 nodes while investigating.

jordan: I can flip kill-switch flag: `redwoodctl feature disable batching-heuristic-v2`

lee: before we flip, any customer-facing risk on toggle (stateful)? kill-switch is safe and instantaneous.

katie: notify SRE and CS about possible customer impact. I'll draft a short note for status page.

sam: go ahead jordan. execute now.

jordan: ran:
```
# executed at 1951235008
redwoodctl feature disable batching-heuristic-v2 --env canary
Result: OK
```

jordan: feature disabled. monitoring...

incident-bot: Metric update: p99 decreased from 1.4s -> 420ms in 45s after kill-switch. Errors down to 0.25%.

maya: good. continue with routing rollback for canary binary to v2.1.6 build id b-914. sam want me to do rollout-controller rollback?

sam: yes. prefer rollback to stable binary for canary only, keep rollout paused for prod. jordan can you run the traffic reroute job?

jordan: running reroute: `redwoodctl rollout revert canary --to b-914 --reason "latency regression"`

devops-bot: Deployment event: canary revert started at 1951235233 by jordan.

jordan: revert completed at 1951235278. health checks green.

incident-bot: Post-action metrics: p99 ~210ms, throughput back to 98% of baseline. No customers showing sustained 5xx counts.

lee: digging into root cause: the new heuristic introduced a path that bypasses optimized CUDA kernels when batch merge logic sees >N small partial batches; combined with a race in KV cache invalidation we hit fallback path. On some GPU kernels the fallback is 6-7x slower.

sam: so two contributing issues: batching heuristic bug + KV cache invalidation timing. Both triggered under the canary traffic distribution.

maya: customer impact: brief spike of elevated latency and small percentage of 503/500 for ~6 minutes during canary ramp. No major accounts reported degraded service yet but CS flagged two customers with elevated error rates (acme-inc, beta-startup).

katie: I've posted to status.redwood.ai: "Brief latency spike and small error rate following canary; rollback to stable binary completed and mitigations applied. Investigating root cause." Will update timeline.

sam: immediate next steps: 1) keep rollout paused 2) hotfix branch to revert batching heuristic change and add extra guard for KV invalidation 3) extended testing on canary traffic pattern simulator 4) run additional perf regression tests including worst-case small-batch workloads 5) postmortem + customer comms.

jordan: I'll open PR for hotfix (branch: hotfix/batching-kv-fix) and attach perf logs.

lee: action items for infra: add metric to detect kernel fallback_count and alert earlier. also add a quick rollback playbook in runbook.

maya: I'll coordinate postmortem and include timeline, logs, and a mitigation checklist. plan to add a follow-up incident update at 1951237140 (30m).

sam: good work. keep channel updated if anything changes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident note saved. Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring.
